etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French vendre, from Old French vendre, from Latin vendere, from vēnum (“(something for) sale”) + dare (“to give”).

definitions.definition: Synonym of sell, now especially to sell through a vending machine.

quote.citation: 1992 September 9, Trish Hall, “Vending Machines, the Next Generation in Dining”, in The New York Times‎[2], →ISSN:
quote.text: Vending has been slow to change partly because the business for years could depend on what it called the four C's: cold drinks, candy, confections and cigarettes.

quote.citation: 2020 October 6, Saritha Rai, “Amazon Launches Month-Long Sale in Battle for Indian Wallets”, in Bloomberg.com‎[3]:
quote.text: Amazon said over 20,000 small stores have signed on to its Local Shops program over five months to vend basics like household essentials and fresh flowers.

definitions.definition: (programming, transitive, uncommon) To provide or export functionality, especially from an API.

quote.citation: 2002, Ravi Mendis, WebObjects Developer's Guide, Sams Publishing, →ISBN, page 289:
quote.text: As you've seen, vending FO documents is pretty straightforward from WebObjects. It is just like vending HTML, XHTML, or SVG.

definitions.definition: The act of vending or selling; a sale.
(UK, Australia, dated) The total sales of coal from a colliery.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Old Norse vend. Compare wynn.

definitions.definition: The letter Ꝩ/ꝩ, used in Old Norse, related to the rune wynn (ᚹ, whence also Latin-script Ƿ/ƿ) but with the bowl open at the top, like a y.

quote.citation: 1874, Richard Cleasby, Gudbrand Vigfusson, An Icelandic-English Dictionary, page 707:
quote.text: [...] a gramm. term, implying the use of the old letter 'vend' in spelling v-rungu, v-rangr, v-reiðr, see introduction to letter R; ...

quote.citation: 2005, Diana L. Paxson, Taking Up The Runes: A Complete Guide To Using Runes In Spells, Rituals, Divination, And Magic, Weiser Books, →ISBN, page 88:
quote.text: In Old English, the meaning of wynn is the same. In Old Norse, the etymological equivalents of words beginning with w are spelled with a v, the letter named “vend” in the Icelandic alphabet.
